title: System Integration
equation: Quality = Systems Working Together ÷ Total Systems
hook: My business was growing and my health was falling apart. That's not a win, that's a trade.
statement: Your work and life systems have to run as one machine. One part winning shouldn't break another.
explainer: Each system can look fine on its own while quietly hurting the others. Longer work hours look great until your sleep and focus fall apart and output drops anyway.
sop: Map your major systems across business and life: health, work, money, relationships.
Spot where progress in one is costing you in another.
Count Systems Working Together against your Total Systems.
Fix the worst conflict by changing timing, ownership, or priority.
Aim for the whole machine running well, not one high score.
equation_example: 4 Systems Working Together out of 6 Total Systems. 4 ÷ 6 = 67%. Higher means most of your systems back each other up. Lower means some are quietly undercutting the others, even if each looks fine.
question: Picture your life as one machine. Write down where it's most out of sync.
closing_statement: A system optimized alone can still break the whole.
caption:
Principle Nº 149: System Integration
